title: Choose the new Moments visual world
question: I recommend Proof Sheet for the simplest, most content-led experience. Keep it, choose an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Proof Sheet
options.lineage: photo-lab contact sheets and grease-pencil selects
options.thesis: A shared roll for two, where every moment reads as the one frame worth keeping.
options.viewport: A quiet title row leads into one generous latest moment, with compact sender context and only real reactions visible; long-press opens a native reaction sheet.
options.risk: Can feel clinical if the spacing, copy, and select mark do not carry enough warmth.

options.label: Seasonal Folio
options.thesis: The relationship unfolds as a sequence of carefully observed daily changes.
options.viewport: A single moment sits like a specimen plate, with date and sender annotations aligned beneath it.
options.risk: Fuses partially because life stages imply progression the product does not actually track.
options.case: High emotional recognition, but lower product clarity than Proof Sheet.

options.label: Memory Box
options.lineage: stacked archive boxes with indexed end labels
options.thesis: Moments become a tactile private archive that opens one memory at a time.
options.viewport: The latest moment slides from a compact labeled stack, while older moments remain indexed below.
options.risk: Fuses poorly because archive-box navigation makes an immediate sharing tool feel stored and collectible.
options.case: Distinctive structure, but weaker immediacy and couple identification.

options.label: Private Broadcast
options.lineage: three-digit teletext magazines on a fixed character grid
options.thesis: Each new moment arrives like a private broadcast intended for one viewer.
options.viewport: A numbered latest-moment page fills the screen with direct SEND and REACT states on the fixed grid.
options.risk: Fuses poorly because its broadcast character overwhelms intimacy and native familiarity.
options.case: Very clear state, but far lower emotional identification than Proof Sheet.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished private photo feed with rounded cards, a familiar bottom bar, and restrained branding.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional app bar, chronological card feed, and persistent compose destination.
canonCard.risk: Immediately familiar, but less memorable and less specific to Moments.
